'''R2-X2''' was the [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series]] [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] used by [[Theron Nett/Legends|Theron Nett]], known as "[[Red Ten/Legends|Red Ten]]," during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. He was destroyed when Nett's [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighter]] was shot down by [[TIE pilot]] [[DS-61-3|"Backstabber"]].<ref name="ANH"></ref><ref name="CCGR2" />

A typical [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] assistant, R2-X2 carried ten coordinates for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jumps, built-in tools, and a computer interface.<ref name="CCGR2" />

==Behind the scenes==
R2-X2 first appeared as a toy in [[Hasbro]]'s [https://www.rebelscum.com/TSCastroS2.asp Astromech Droid Pack Series II] (2006, #87057), which was an exclusive set offered through online retailer Entertainment Earth. The character was reissued in 2009 on a single-figure card ([https://www.rebelscum.com/TLCBD52R2X2.asp #88884]), with an updated, more accurate dark green paint job. An astromech droid in a [[2014]] [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] set was identified as R2-X2 (and Theron Nett's Astromech) in a display at that year's San Diego Comic Con.<ref name="FBTB">{{WebCite|url=https://www.fbtb.net/lego-star-wars/2014/07/24/sdcc-the-lego-star-wars-minifigure-gallery|text=SDCC - The LEGO Star Wars Minifigure Gallery at FBTB.net|archivedate=20200929031301}}</ref>
